thread:
Anya: quick RFC follow-up — we're seeing a lot of tiny queue fragments from bursty mobile clients. fragmentation reduces batching efficiency and spikes token cost. proposing an adaptive 'drain token' to let tiny slices coalesce briefly before dispatch.

Sam: can you sketch the token semantics? sounds like delay-based batching, worried about added p99.

Anya: not just a fixed delay. tokens are issued per lane when occupancy < low_watermark. token extends the slice deadline by up to T ms or until a size threshold is hit. token cancels on large request or if cumulative wait > S ms. goal: merge tiny fragments without penalizing steady streams.

Ben: +1 on the problem. metric suggestion to quantify impact: fragmentation_index = 1 - (sum(batch_size) / sum(capacity_at_time)). gives a sense of wasted headroom. track along with wasted_cycles/ms and per-tenant delta.

Ben: quick pseudocode for metric:
```
frag = 1.0 - (sum(batch_size) / sum(capacity_at_time))
// capacity_at_time = max_batch_size * num_dispatches_at_time
```

Maya: flag: delaying can hold KV cache refs and block eviction. token should be kvcache-aware — shorten or drop if kvcache miss rate rises. also ensure tokens don't persist across host restart.

Anya: agreed. plan to tag tokens with {ttl_ms, kvcache_guard, tenant_affinity}. kvcache_guard shortens ttl when miss_rate_delta > threshold. tokens should be in-memory only.

Sam: preemption question: if a high-priority request arrives, token must be preemptible instantly. also need fast-path bypass for latency-critical tiny requests (e.g., auth).

Anya: yep — token respects lane preempt signal. fast-path: if request.meta.latency_sensitive == true or size < micro_threshold then bypass token and go microqueue.

Ben: did a small sim locally. cmd: `./scripts/sim_queue --pattern bursty --token 5ms`. results: throughput +7%, p50 stable, p99 improved -8% for bulk tenants, small latency regressions for ultra-low-latency clients if not exempted.

infra-bot: canary sim job queued: job id 876543. logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/876543 :white_check_mark:

Maya: also consider edge error modes: token held during GC or host restart; token must not be persisted to lease metadata. ensure token expiry triggers immediate release of any KV refs.

Anya: next steps: 1) add fragmentation_index telemetry + dashboard 2) implement drain-token prototype behind tenant flag 3) run canary sim and targeted microbench across latency_sensitive tag. volunteers?

Sam: I'll take telemetry + dashboard.

Ben: I'll prototype token code and the sim harness (this week).

Maya: I'll audit kvcache interactions and migration risks.

Anya: thanks — I'll file follow-up RFC note and put the tracker task: https://r.rw/frag-drain-123 :thumbsup:
